bug_semantics: An unauthenticated WebUI userpass login first resolves the submitted username to an account. A username with no mapping returns an account/identity-not-found page, while a mapped username with a wrong password proceeds to token authentication and returns a different token/authentication failure page. The response content therefore reveals whether the submitted username exists.
flaw_origin: Commit b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f introduced the WebUI userpass login flow in lib/rucio/web/ui/common/utils.py. Its new log_in function called identity.list_accounts_for_identity, returned 'No accounts for the given identity.' when the result was empty, and only attempted get_auth_token_user_pass for a mapped identity, whose exception returned 'Cannot get auth token'. Later refactors made the text more explicit and ported the same branch structure to Flask, but did not originate the observable discrepancy.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f shows author Ruturaj <ruturaj2305@gmail.com>, committer Ruturaj <ruturaj2305@gmail.com>, and the sole message 'WebUI: Resolve Conflicts'; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer in the BIC commit object.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-38wq-6q2w-hcf9 identifies /ui/login response content as the oracle: an unmapped identity receives 'Cannot get find any account associated with ... identity', whereas a mapped identity with a wrong password receives 'Cannot get auth token ...'. It declares patched boundaries 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1.

git log -L over userpass_auth in lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py traced the Flask implementation to d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605, but its parent already contained the same userpass decision and distinct errors in lib/rucio/web/ui/common/utils.py. Continuing git log -L over the legacy userpass_auth and log_in functions reached b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f as the first commit that wrote the mechanism; ef0342ad5bd298b1bb829b9193fea5576271d193 was a later refactor and d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605 was a later Flask port, so neither is the BIC.

git show b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f:lib/rucio/web/ui/common/utils.py shows the new log_in flow at approximately lines 158-226: list_accounts_for_identity(data.username, 'userpass'), an immediate 'No accounts for the given identity.' response for an empty result, and a separate 'Cannot get auth token' response around get_auth_token_user_pass for mapped identities.

Immediate-parent verification was direct: git grep for '^def log_in', 'No accounts for the given identity', and 'Cannot get auth token' in e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc:lib/rucio/web/ui/common/utils.py returned no matches; a separate git grep for get_auth_token_user_pass under that parent's lib/rucio/web/ui tree also returned no matches. git cat-file -p confirms e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc is the BIC's sole immediate parent.

Version ancestry is consistent with the advisory: git tag --contains b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f begins in the 1.21 release series, and git merge-base --octopus of the BIC with tags 35.8.2, 38.5.3, and 39.3.0 returns the BIC itself, proving all three last-vulnerable boundaries contain the originating mechanism.

The direct upstream remediation 0b22b350201bcf040aa1aade476cf69944019d97 changes lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py so both a missing account and a failed token resolve to the same generic 'Authentication failed' response. Stable patch-id 5a814d04e90425e50502170b13aa61d42f9de09b proves its release-line equivalents are 33bc01dc055c8e52a688404068419c916fab797f, 949ff8cfd7efb51c71cdceb5e80be8f6858e0b73, and 1ea6771b43c7ae45485486692189e40fbe61f496.

git tag --contains shows those three direct backports first appear respectively in 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1, not the preceding vulnerable tags. The follow-up 46e0e1012ff404fda157a80f3d249bc9162b09dd genericizes the remaining multi-VO validation errors; stable patch-id 79c6223b3ced3258e26ec08d9b9b0c604c2904d3 matches backports 7a94b9875e3bbae3b53ef9f9d33be2c9ae257fde, 92db5b15b7628d289836670679ef87b3bc5bd04e, and 4178a1ccf1a0768c53c5ab465dc4c98e4206c552, each also contained in the corresponding first-patched tag. Release references: https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/35.8.3, https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/38.5.4, and https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/39.3.1.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the response oracle, not merely the final wording. The earliest causal mechanism is the 2019 userpass handler added by b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f: it branches on identity existence before password authentication and exposes different failures. The immediate parent has neither that handler nor a userpass-token call under the WebUI, so parent absence is proven. Subsequent commits preserved and clarified the behavior: ef0342ad5bd298b1bb829b9193fea5576271d193 restructured it, multi-VO work extended it, and d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605 ported it to Flask. Those are refactor/extension/port commits rather than origin commits. Upstream fix 0b22b350201bcf040aa1aade476cf69944019d97 removes the existence-dependent early response and uses a common failure path, with patch-equivalent backports at every advisory boundary; the follow-up genericizes the remaining VO-validation variants. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a squash aggregate requiring member reconstruction. Its commit object contains only a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
